title: Sidewall spacer passivated epitaxial NbN/AlN/NbN Josephson junctions for superconducting qubit applications
authors: Koki Honda, Daiki Kurihara, Hiroki Kutsuma, Hirotaka Terai, Taro Yamashita
abstract: Epitaxial NbN/AlN/NbN Josephson junctions are promising alternatives to conventional Al/AlO$_x$/Al junctions for superconducting qubits due to their crystalline tunnel barriers and the high transition temperature of NbN. However, their integration into quantum circuits typically requires complex fabrication processes involving amorphous interlayer dielectrics, which can degrade qubit coherence times. To address these issues, we developed sidewall spacer passivated epitaxial NbN/AlN/NbN junctions using a fabrication process that reduces both the volume of amorphous dielectric material and fabrication complexity. The fabricated junctions exhibited a large gap voltage of approximately 5.6 mV and low subgap leakage currents. By varying the thickness of the AlN tunnel barrier, high-quality junctions were fabricated over a wide range of critical current densities ${\it J}_c$, from 0.3 to 10$^4$ A/cm$^2$. In addition, the comparison of the current-voltage characteristics before and after buffered hydrofluoric acid treatment indicated that the wet etching process did not degrade the electrical characteristics of the junctions. These results establish a scalable fabrication process for epitaxial Josephson junctions and provide a promising platform for high-coherence nitride-based superconducting qubits.
summary: This paper reports on a novel, scalable fabrication method for epitaxial NbN/AlN/NbN Josephson junctions designed for superconducting qubits. By implementing a sidewall spacer passivation technique, the authors overcome issues associated with amorphous dielectrics, achieving junctions with high quality and tunable critical current densities. This establishes a promising platform for building high-coherence quantum processors.
main_problem: Developing a scalable fabrication process for epitaxial Josephson junctions for superconducting qubits that minimizes amorphous dielectric material and fabrication complexity, which typically degrade qubit coherence times.
main_result: The developed sidewall spacer passivation process yields high-quality epitaxial NbN/AlN/NbN junctions with excellent electrical characteristics and wide tunability of critical current density.
method: The authors fabricated the junctions using a multi-step process involving reactive DC magnetron sputtering, sidewall spacer passivation, and anisotropic etching, followed by electrical characterization.
model_or_system: The physical system is the epitaxial NbN/AlN/NbN Josephson junction, which serves as the core element for superconducting qubits. The performance is characterized by its Josephson energy ($E_J$) and charging energy ($E_C$).
key_observables: Large gap voltage ($\approx 5.6 	ext{ mV}$), low subgap leakage currents, and a wide range of controllable critical current densities ($J_c$: $0.3$ to $10^4 	ext{ A/cm}^2$).
important_parameters: The critical current density ($J_c$) is highly tunable by varying the thickness of the AlN tunnel barrier, following an exponential relationship.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the sidewall spacer passivation process successfully mitigates coherence degradation caused by amorphous dielectrics and complex fabrication steps.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the complex fabrication process using a sidewall spacer. Figure 2 shows the measured current-voltage characteristics for different AlN barrier thicknesses. Figure 3 demonstrates the exponential dependence of $J_c$ on the AlN barrier thickness.
paper_structure: The paper details the fabrication process (including sidewall passivation) to create epitaxial NbN/AlN/NbN junctions. It then presents electrical characterization, showing the wide tunability of $J_c$ and confirming the robustness of the junctions against wet etching.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses the hardware limitations (fabrication complexity and coherence loss) in superconducting qubit platforms, which is central to quantum information science.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Fabrication process and cross-sectional SEM image of an NbN/AlN/NbN trilayer junction with the sidewall spacer structure: (a) An NbN/AlN/NbN trilayer is deposited on an MgO (100) substrate. (b) The trilayer is patterned and etched by chlorine-based ICP-RIE. (c) A SiO2 layer is deposited by CVD. (d) A sidewall spacer is formed by anisotropic etching of the SiO2 layer with a gas mixture of Ar, CF4, and CHF3. (e) An NbN wiring layer is deposited. (f) The wiring and counter-electrode layers are etched by fluorine-based RIE, thereby defining the junction area. (g) Cross-sectional SEM image of the fabricated junction.

Figure 2: Current–voltage characteristics of NbN/AlN/NbN tunnel junctions with different AlN barrier thicknesses, measured at 2.3 K: (a) 1.27 nm, (b) 1.54 nm, (c) 1.77 nm, and (d) 2.09 nm. AlN thicknesses were estimated from the AlN deposition rate and deposition time.

Figure 3: Dependence of the critical current density Jc on the AlN barrier thickness dAlN. The values of dAlN were estimated from the AlN deposition rate and deposition time. The solid line represents an exponential fit to the experimental data.
